Save ₹4,302/yr in costs. Raise debt from 1% → 21%. Est. tax impact: ₹19,675.'.

minor.issue: On live priyankamantri plan (26 MFs), improvements.overlap_pct = {before:95.8, after:95.8} — no reduction. Root cause: plan emits 5 REGULAR_DIRECT_DUPLICATE exits (reason_codes) but _compute_improvements only counts OVERLAP_CONSOLIDATION / UNDERPERFORMER_REPLACEMENT for overlap reduction, so regular→direct switches (which do keep the same fund exposure) correctly aren't counted. BUT then overlap_pct shows 0 improvement even though the plan claims to improve the portfolio. Consider either (a) dropping overlap_pct from summary when delta=0, or (b) estimating residual after switch target selection.

improvements.top_amc_pct before/after are both 0 for priyankamantri even though she has 26 MFs. Root cause: portfolio_intelligence.amc_exposure is empty (not populated) when building the plan. Non-blocking, but undermines the AMC concentration narrative in plan_summary.

Rule 7 Do-Nothing gating uses `a.get('priority') == 'high'` (string) to detect high-priority actions, but live actions are emitted with INTEGER priority (1, 2, 3, …). As a result, if portfolio_score ≥ 75, Rule 7 would erroneously fire even when integer-priority high actions exist. Either normalize priority to a string, or compare against 1 / {'high','HIGH',1}. Currently masked by score=64.2 < 75 on the test user.

rca of the issue: No critical bugs. One latent issue documented: priority type mismatch in Rule 7 gate (string 'high' compared against integer action.priority). Non-triggering today because live portfolio_score=64.2 < 75. Reproduction requires seeding a healthy portfolio (score≥75) with at least one int-priority=1 action — Rule 7 would wrongly set do_nothing=true and emit a HOLD action. Mitigation: define `_priority_is_high(a) -> bool` returning `a.get('priority') in ('high','HIGH',1)` and use throughout.
